newsitem.title: KENYA: More than 160 children return to southern Sudan.
newsitem.headline: More than 160 children return to southern Sudan.

text.p: More than 160 south Sudanese children are being reunited with their parents after three years in the first family reunification in areas controlled by the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).

The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) said in a statement on Friday that 168 children were being reunited with their parents in southern Sudan after living in a camp for unaccompanied minors in New Cush, Kenya, for over a year.
They arrived in New Cush in June 1995 after an arduous two-year journey by foot from southern Sudan to Uganda and back again either fleeing fighting in the south or seeking education.
"I want to attend school," said Albino Aguto from a small village near Adior in southern Sudan, where a group of children arrived by U.N. plane on Thursday from northwestern Kenya.
"If there is a nice school, I will stay until the highest grade. I will refuse to go into the army. I can't fight...Even the gun is too heavy for me because I'm still small," he said.
UNICEF said the greatest challenge for the agency was to ensure that schools in southern Sudan were functioning so that the children would not leave their families again.
The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy or independence of the mainly Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arabised north.
